purpose: Defines the strict Pydantic v2 schema for the eight non-strategy YAML config files and the single loader that reads, hashes and validates them (load_all, line 2552), returning one AppConfig (line 2515) that main.py and the subsystems listed in the manifest's imported_by are handed by dependency injection. purpose: Single in-process ledger of capital for this trading system: it holds `_total` plus a per-bucket (intraday/positional) split of available/reserved/used, and every capital mutation in the system goes through its reserve/release/commit_to_used/release_used methods (lines 521, 637, 894, 1204). Each mutation writes one row to the `fm_ledger` table BEFORE touching in-memory state (write-ahead, `_write_ledger` line 2520), then re-checks the identity available+reserved+used == total (`_check_invariant` line 2391) and, on a break, fires `kill_switch.hard_kill` from outside the lock (line 2495). It is consumed by capital.position_sizer, capital.risk_engine, main, orders.eod_squareoff, orders.order_placer, orders.order_reconciler and signals.signal_processor, which also borrow its RLock via `portfolio_lock` (line 426) so approve+reserve is one critical section.

purpose: Implements the 15:17 IST end-of-day square-off sequence for this system: it cancels pending intraday entry orders and live SL/TGT exit legs, then exits every open MIS/CO position (CO by cancelling the entry bracket, MIS by MARKET or aggressive-LIMIT-then-MARKET), writes one eod_squareoff_log row per fire, publishes EodSquareoffComplete, resets fund_manager daily PnL and sends the Telegram DAILY SUMMARY. It is driven by an external poller (main.py calls check_and_fire(now)); it deliberately never touches CNC/delivery positions and never waits for fill confirmations, handing fills to order_monitor. It also owns restart recovery: on post_wire_init() it inspects today's log row and may fire late (IN_PROGRESS crash, or no row while past EOD but before market close).

purpose: Implements the system-wide trading halt used as the last-mile gate before any order: three states (INACTIVE / SOFT_KILL / HARD_KILL, :175-179) held in memory behind an RLock (:284) and persisted to a single kill_switch_state row (:966) persist-first so a failed write aborts the state change. Its importers (main, orders.order_placer, orders.order_reconciler, orders.eod_squareoff, capital.fund_manager, capital.drift_handler, scripts.clear_kill_switch, scripts.system_manager) call is_active(intent) (:510) to block entries/exits, soft_kill()/hard_kill() to trip it, and clear_stale_state()/auto_clear_scheduled_kill() at boot (:315, :366) to clear yesterday's or a scheduled kill. On HARD_KILL with an adapter injected it also PERFORMS the flatten itself: it dispatches a non-daemon worker thread (:1193) that runs _exit_all_trades_indestructible (:1670) -- cancel resting SL/TGT, cancel CO brackets, place marketable-LIMIT exits, sweep orphan broker positions, retry with backoff until a 2h deadline.

purpose: A read-only library of pre-trading boot checks that main.py calls in Phase 0c/0d: it classifies the startup into COLD/WARM/CRASH/HALT from the session row plus kill_switch state (line 192), then runs individual checks (clock vs broker, NTP drift, config-file presence, config-hash diff, scanner URL reachability, local webhook /health, instrument-cache size, strategy YAML validity, holiday calendar, kiteconnect version pin, TEMP markers, disk space, DB file permissions) and aggregates them into one StartupReport with `blocking_failures` and `warnings` (line 1508). It takes every dependency as a parameter (state_store, kill_switch, time_authority, broker_adapter, app_config, http_fetcher_fn) and its header states it performs no state mutations and no process control (lines 10-12, 31-36) -- the caller decides what to do with ok=False. Two of its checks break that read-only rule by raising StartupCheckFailed (lines 1003, 1059).

purpose: The single SQLite gateway for this system's persistent runtime state: it owns connection setup (WAL, synchronous FULL, foreign_keys ON, 30s busy_timeout — lines 107-113), the schema-version gate and migration permission gate on open (lines 398, 420-427), an explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction context manager (line 531), and roughly 100 hand-written query/write helpers used by capital.fund_manager, capital.kill_switch, capital.risk_engine, main, orders.eod_squareoff, orders.order_manager, orders.order_reconciler, reports.daily_report, reports.daily_trade_review and scripts.backfill_closure_source_w8 (manifest importers). Its helpers encode the system's operational definitions rather than plumbing only — e.g. which trade statuses count as 'executed' for the daily cap (_EXECUTED_TRADE_STATUSES, line 734), how a DELIVERY trade is identified (ENTRY-leg orders.product = 'CNC', line 874), and the atomic once-only status flips that decide whether capital is released twice (lines 1794, 2423). The module deliberately contains no business math, no alerting and no broker access; the only non-SQLite act is a best-effort CRITICAL sentinel file written when a migration is refused (lines 344-352).

purpose: Worker pool that drains the receiver's signal_queue and runs each queued signal through the admission pipeline: PROCESSING status write, kill-switch / entry-window / 60s-age / shadow-inning pre-flight, scanner->strategy lookup via scan_webhook_map, strategy-control verdict, secondary screener, entry+SL derivation, optional momentum fresh-LTP re-anchor, position sizing, then (inside fund_manager.portfolio_lock) per-strategy cap + one-trade-per-symbol-direction + risk approve + capital reserve, then entry throttle and order_placer.place(). It owns orchestration and status bookkeeping only; every decision is delegated to injected objects (screener, sizer, risk_engine, fund_manager, kill_switch, order_placer). Its importers are main (the live wiring) and ten unit/integration test modules; it also exposes three alternative entry points used by other components: continue_from_gate (EntryGate PRICE_HIT, line 2063), continue_from_retest (RetestMonitor CONFIRMED, line 2428) and admit_prepared/reject_prepared (the PortfolioAllocator enforce worker, lines 1699 and 1759).

CHECK9 computes should_alert with bypass_backoff=True, and _should_alert_for_discrepancy returns True unconditionally on that flag (line 558-559). exit_source is derived from `exit_price != entry_price`, not from which source answered. A price that came from the LTP fallback (1660-1665) is still labelled "broker_trades", and a genuine broker-trades price that equals entry_price is labelled "entry_proxy". CHECK4 keeps only `.cancelled` from the OrphanLegOutcome and drops mid_fill / ambiguous / read_failed — the three facts D1 (lines 139-149) introduced the dataclass to preserve. On the partial-close path a mid-filling own leg and a failed read are again indistinguishable from 'no orphan legs'.

`except Exception: remaining = None` swallows the read failure with no log, and the following guard `if remaining is not None and len(remaining) == 0` then silently skips the cancel-safety naked re-check (N5) that the docstring at 3514-3517 promises.

`except Exception: return None` in the oversell detector swallows any DB error with no log line, so a query failure is indistinguishable from 'no matching closed trade' and the position is treated as a human order instead.
`except Exception: pass` swallows the idempotency read in the ENTRY backfill; if get_orders_for_trade raises, the function proceeds to insert a second ENTRY row rather than skipping.

purpose: Single orchestration entry point: parses CLI args, refuses to start on a non-trading day or outside the 08:00-18:15 IST START window, loads config, opens the StateStore (the only sanctioned schema migrator, main.py:2241-2245), constructs and wires ~40 subsystems (broker adapter, fund manager, risk engine, screeners, signal processor, order placer/monitor/reconciler, EOD and MIS square-off, webhook server, health server), runs startup checks and a synchronous startup reconcile, then blocks on a shutdown event and tears everything down in reverse order. It is invoked as a service/cron process (main.py:4321-4329); the listed importers (scripts.sr_level_export and 9 test modules) import it as a module to call individual helpers rather than to boot the system.

purpose: The single wrapper around the kiteconnect SDK: every broker call in the system goes through this class, and the module docstring states no other module imports kiteconnect (lines 5-7, ZA1 at 10-11). It validates order arguments, takes a rate-limiter token per category, resolves a semantic intent to a broker product code, registers/transitions the order state machine, calls kite, and translates kiteconnect exceptions into the system's BrokerError family; it also carries a full in-memory paper simulator (orders, fills, positions, GTTs, holdings, capital) so the same public surface serves paper mode. Its importers are main, broker.order_monitor, orders.eod_squareoff, orders.order_protocol_co, orders.order_protocol_limit and scripts/tests (manifest hint).

defects.what: PlacedOrder.status is documented as "SUBMITTED" | "PENDING" (paper), but no code path ever sets "PENDING": the live path hardcodes status="SUBMITTED" (678) and the paper path does the same (2195). The "PENDING" value can never appear.

PlacedOrder carries no success/failure field at all (fields 142-153): a caller holding a PlacedOrder cannot distinguish an accepted order from one the broker later rejected; the only signal is an exception at placement time.

Paper modify_order returns ModifyResult(success=True) without touching _paper_fills, so a paper price/trigger modification never changes the stored order record that get_open_orders (1893) and get_all_orders (1952) report -- they keep echoing the values written at placement (2166).

Paper cancel_order returns success=True unconditionally; the status write is guarded by `if broker_order_id in self._paper_fills` (1045), so cancelling an unknown id reports success while get_order_history still returns the default "SUBMITTED" (1169).

Live cancel_order swallows every Exception into CancelResult(success=False, reason=str(exc)) via the bare `except Exception` and log_exception, bypassing _translate_broker_exception -- so a 429 on a cancel never penalizes the bucket (contrast 2052-2056) and a token/auth failure is indistinguishable from a rejection. modify_order does the same at 1141-1147. Neither path calls _reset_429_attempts on success.

The "unknown order_type" fallback `return price` in _ltp_satisfies_condition is unreachable from the public path: _validate_place_order admits only MARKET/LIMIT/SL/SL-M (2101-2105) and _compute_ltp_gated_fill_price handles MARKET itself (2445) before calling, so only LIMIT/SL-M/SL ever reach here and all three are handled above.

get_quote_raw tags the operation "get_quote_raw", which is absent from _CATEGORY_MAP, so _translate_broker_exception's `_CATEGORY_MAP.get(operation, "order")` (2053) falls back to "order": a 429 on a raw quote penalizes the ORDER bucket rather than the quote bucket. get_live_margin_pct has the same shape with operation "order_margins" (1610), which is also absent from the map.

get_gtt's paper branch returns dict(rec), a SHALLOW copy: the nested "condition" dict and "orders" list are the same objects held in _paper_gtts, so a caller mutating them mutates adapter state despite the docstring's "a copy of the stored record" (917-918). get_gtts has the same shallow copy at 938.

purpose: Single orchestrator for one trade's whole order lifecycle: place() (line 871) creates the trades row, runs the last-mile gates (kill-switch, EOD cutoff, entry-slippage, margin top-up, liquidity), calls FullEntryEngine.execute (1345) for the ENTRY leg only, persists the order rows and registers each leg with OrderMonitor plus an in-memory _fill_map. It then handles the resulting events it subscribed to at construction (693, 697, 700): on ENTRY fill it commits the capital reservation, records the fill and places the deferred SL/TGT at the ACTUAL filled qty (2156-2171); on SL/TGT/EOD fill it closes the trade, cancels the OCO sibling and releases used capital (2275-2526). Its callers are main.py (wiring), signals.signal_processor (the only production caller of place()), core.config_auditor (imports the pure validator at 279) and the unit/integration tests listed in the manifest.

purpose: The in-memory, thread-safe authority for order state. It owns a 9-state set, a one-way transition table in which the four terminal states have no exits, and refuses every illegal move with InvalidTransitionError. purpose: Background watchdog that polls the broker's profile endpoint every check_interval_sec during market hours to confirm the Zerodha access token is still valid. purpose: The PRIMARY MIS safety orchestrator added alongside (never replacing) the 15:15 SOFT_KILL and the 15:17 EOD routine: one daemon poll thread runs two passes — PASS_1 at cutoff-first_offset and PASS_2 at cutoff-second_offset — that find open equity-MIS broker positions, cancel that symbol's resting MIS SL/TGT legs, verify the cancel at the broker, then submit a protected MARKET exit before Zerodha's earliest CAS auto-square-off. It carries the 03/04-Sep incident fixes: F1 restores the stop on every failure path, F2 polls the cancel to a bounded deadline, F1b verifies that a restored stop is actually resting, and Block A blocks PASS_2 while a PASS_1 order is unresolved. Imported by main.

purpose: An in-memory, thread-safe entry-rate limiter used by signals/signal_processor.py (constructed at signal_processor.py:265, called at signal_processor.py:1463, :2278 and :2583) to stop bursts of entry placements. Three gates are evaluated global-first inside one lock: a minimum seconds gap between any two placed entries (:78), a rolling-window burst cap (:86), and a per-symbol cooldown (:98). admit() is deliberately a single atomic check-AND-record call (:65, record at :110-113) rather than a split check/record pair, so concurrent worker threads cannot all pass a check before any of them records.

defects.what: The timeout is evaluated before the candles are folded, so once elapsed_sec exceeds timeout_sec the function reports REJECT/"timeout" even if the supplied candles contain a completed confirmation sequence.

purpose: The screening orchestrator for main/signal_processor: it fetches a quote, builds the market_data dict, applies the optional MIS learned-blocklist pre-drop and the pre-fill circuit-proximity reject, runs the ten steps through step_executor, scores them with quality_scorer, applies the per-strategy min_score override, and persists exactly one verdict per signal (P18). It also carries the V3 Hard-Gate paths: `off` (default, byte-identical legacy), `shadow` (logs OLD vs NEW) and `enforce` (gate first, 8 scored steps, re-scaled thresholds).

defects.what: `date` and `Decimal` are imported but never used anywhere in the file.
DEFAULT_CIRCUIT_MARGIN_PCT is imported with a long justifying comment but never referenced after the rule was relocated to hard_gate; the import line is its only occurrence in the file.
Both state_store writes share one try whose except only logs, so a locked DB or full disk silently loses the whole screening verdict; the comment at 646-649 acknowledges the swallow.

In enforce mode with a hard_gate but no scoring_config, `_step_weights` is {} and rescaled_total then returns 0 for every signal (hard_gate.py:192), so every gate survivor becomes REJECTED_SCORE_0 while the enforce branch is still taken at 202.

A per-strategy min_score of 20 or less rescales to 0 (hard_gate.py:212); because the fallback to _v3_min_pass only triggers when min_score <= 0, eff_min becomes 0 and the `total < eff_min` test can never reject.

The evidence-failure recovery calls `.note_failure` on the result of `getattr(self, "_evidence", None)`, which raises AttributeError precisely when the recorder is None; the surrounding try swallows it, so the recovery is a no-op in the case it guards.
market_data_snapshot is only a shallow dict copy, so nested values shared with the live market_data are not isolated from later mutation.
